etymology: Old English uppan, on, on top of. Webster 1828: resting or being on the top or surface; then, in a state of resting or dependence. The KJV uses it for the Spirit moving upon the face of the waters, for blessing upon a people, for the Spirit of the Lord GOD upon the Anointed, and for the Holy Ghost coming upon Mary and upon the witnesses.
biblical_def: Upon in Scripture is not a vague spiritual atmosphere. It names where a weight, a Person, or a word actually rests. Creation opens with it: darkness was upon the face of the deep, and the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters (Gen 1:2). That is not mood. That is God over the unformed. David locates blessing the same way: thy blessing is upon thy people (Ps 3:8). Isaiah’s Servant speaks as One who has been marked: The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me; because the LORD hath anointed me (Isa 61:1). The angel does not offer Mary a feeling; he names a coming: The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee (Luke 1:35). Pentecost is the same grammar: ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you (Acts 1:8). The dictionary therefore will not let upon dissolve into vibe. Blessing rests. Anointing rests. The Spirit comes. The creature does not climb into God; God comes down and takes His place.
webster_summary: Webster 1828 defines UPON as a preposition: resting or being on the top or surface; then dependence, burden, direction, relation, occasion, security, attack, and support. His biblical illustration is attack: The Philistines be upon thee, Samson.
webster_full: UPON', preposition — 1. Resting or being on the top or surface; as being upon a hill, or upon a rock; upon a field; upon a table; upon a river; upon the altar; upon the roof. He has his coat upon his back; his hat is upon his head.

2. In a state of resting or dependence; as upon this condition; he will contract with you upon these terms. Upon our repentance we hope to be forgiven. 3. Denoting resting, as a burden. Impose upon yourself this task.
Webster’s twelfth sense is Scripture’s own: noting approach or attack. The Philistines be upon thee, Samson. Judges 16. The word can rest as blessing or fall as judgment; it is never a fog.
scriptures: Genesis 1:2
And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.
Psalm 3:8
Salvation belongeth unto the LORD: thy blessing is upon thy people. Selah.
Isaiah 61:1

The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me; because the LORD hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek; he hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and the opening of the prison to them that are bound;
Luke 1:35

And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God.
Acts 1:8

But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.
corruption_summary: Upon is corrupted when the Spirit’s coming is recast as a worship mood, when blessing upon a people is sold as a prosperity technique, and when Pentecost is turned into private voltage with the witnesses left out.
corruption_paragraphs: The first corruption is to make Genesis 1:2 a mood board. The Spirit moved upon the face of the waters because God was forming a world, not because the deep had a spiritual atmosphere. Inspirational religion likes hovering language and drops the Creator. The recovery is the first chapter: God speaks, and the Spirit is already there as God.

The second corruption is to treat upon as a lever. Psalm 3:8 is blessing that belongs to the LORD and rests on His people. Prosperity talk turns that rest into a method — speak it, claim it, pull it down. David is not operating a machine. He is confessing whose salvation it is.

The third corruption is to empty Luke 1:35 and Acts 1:8. Continuationist spectacle and therapeutic religion both like power-language and drop the grammar: the Holy Ghost comes upon, and then a holy Child is born, or witnesses are sent. Pentecost is not a private charge. It is the Spirit of Christ taking a people for a public word.
roots_summary: Old English uppan. Verse-cache Strong’s on the quotations below: Greek epi (G1909) at Luke 1:35 and Acts 1:8 (come upon). Genesis 1:2, Psalm 3:8, and Isaiah 61:1 leave the English upon itself untagged in this cache; no Hebrew preposition number is minted for those three. Companion pages treat the Spirit, the anointing, and the incarnation; this page is the English preposition.
roots_lines: Greek epi (G1909) — upon, on, over (Luke 1:35; Acts 1:8, come upon).
Acts 1:8 likewise: come G1904, upon G1909, Holy G40, Ghost G4151.
Genesis 1:2, Psalm 3:8, and Isaiah 61:1 untagged on the word upon in this cache — no Hebrew number is invented.
usage: Darkness was upon the deep, and the Spirit moved upon the waters — God over the unformed, not a vibe over chaos.
Blessing is upon the LORD’s people because salvation belongs to Him (Ps 3:8), not because they pulled it down.
The Holy Ghost comes upon Mary and upon the witnesses (Luke 1:35; Acts 1:8); power here is a Person arriving.

etymology: Old English eallswā: all + so. Webster 1828: likewise; in like manner. His illustration is Matthew 6:21: Where your treasure is, there will your heart be also. The KJV uses it for God’s extra work in creation, for the heart that follows its treasure, for the disciples where Christ is, for heirs glorified with Him, and for the brother who must be loved if God is loved.
biblical_def: Also in Scripture is not a throwaway conjunction. It binds a second thing to the first by the same rule. Genesis does not treat the stars as an afterthought of mood; he made the stars also (Gen 1:16). The same God who ruled day and night with two great lights made the host as well. Jesus will not let the heart pretend independence: where your treasure is, there will your heart be also (Matt 6:21). The place He prepares is not a separate destiny: that where I am, there ye may be also (John 14:3). Union with Christ has a matching clause in suffering and glory: that we may be also glorified together (Rom 8:17). Love of God is not allowed to stop at the vertical: he who loveth God love his brother also (1 John 4:21). The dictionary therefore keeps also from becoming additive religion — one more spiritual accessory. It is the same Lord, the same treasure, the same Christ, the same commandment, arriving at the next lawful place.
webster_summary: Webster 1828 defines ALSO as an adverb from all and so: likewise; in like manner. He quotes Matthew 6:21 as the illustration: Where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
webster_full: AL'SO, adverb [all and so.] Likewise; in like manner.
Where your treasure is, there will your heart be also. Matthew 6:21.
Webster refuses a second heart. The adverb does not add a mood. It locates the same heart where the treasure already is.
scriptures: Genesis 1:16
And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also.
Matthew 6:21
For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
John 14:3
And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and receive you unto myself; that where I am, there ye may be also.
Romans 8:17
And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.
1 John 4:21
And this commandment have we from him, That he who loveth God love his brother also.
corruption_summary: Also is corrupted when it becomes extra-credit religion, when the heart is treated as free of its treasure, and when love of God is allowed to float without the brother.
corruption_paragraphs: The first corruption is additive religion. Genesis 1:16 is not God tacking on décor. The stars are the same day’s work. Therapeutic religion loves also as a second program — Jesus plus a technique, grace plus a brand. The recovery is one Creator and one finished day.

The second corruption is to split treasure from heart. Matthew 6:21 will not permit a compartment. Inspirational talk pretends you can store money, applause, or platform in one place and keep a pure heart in another. Jesus says the heart will be also wherever the treasure already is. The adverb is a verdict, not a motto.

The third corruption is a God-love that will not travel. First John 4:21 makes the brother the test. Sentiment can praise God and despise the man beside it. The commandment does not offer a second, softer love. He who loves God loves his brother also — the same love arriving at the next lawful object.
roots_summary: Old English eallswā (all + so). Verse-cache Strong’s on the quotations below: Greek kai (G2532) at Matthew 6:21, John 14:3, Romans 8:17, and 1 John 4:21. Genesis 1:16 is untagged in this cache; no Hebrew number is invented for he made the stars also. The companion entry likewise already treats the parallel adverb; this page is the English also.
roots_lines: Greek kai (G2532) — and, also, even (Matt 6:21; John 14:3; Rom 8:17; 1 John 4:21).
Romans 8:17 also tags glorified together as syndoxazō (G4888) beside also (G2532).
Genesis 1:16 untagged in this cache — no Hebrew number is minted for also.
usage: He made the stars also (Gen 1:16) — the same God, the same day, not a second religion.
The heart will be also where the treasure is (Matt 6:21); the adverb is a verdict.
He who loves God loves his brother also (1 John 4:21); vertical talk that will not travel is not love.

etymology: Plural of man. Webster 1828: two or more males, individuals of the human race; then males of bravery; then persons, people, mankind in an indefinite sense. The KJV uses the plural for sons of men in their vanity, for nations that are but men, for all men commanded to repent, for the race that needs the one Mediator, and for the charge quit you like men.
biblical_def: Men in Scripture is not a branding exercise and not a slur. It is the plural of the creature God made male, and often the name of the race in its need. David rebukes the sons of men who turn glory into shame and love vanity (Ps 4:2). He asks that the nations know themselves to be but men (Ps 9:20) — not gods, not a law to themselves. The gospel then refuses a boutique audience: God now commandeth all men every where to repent (Acts 17:30). Between that race and God there is not a program but a Person: one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus (1 Tim 2:5). The church is not told to dissolve the noun. It is told to inhabit it: Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong (1 Cor 16:13). The dictionary therefore keeps two things from collapsing. Male is creational. The Man Christ Jesus is the Mediator of men. Courage in that name is not theater. It is the plural learning again to be what God called it, under the one Man who stands for them.
webster_summary: Webster 1828 defines MEN as the plural of man: two or more males, individuals of the human race; then males of bravery; then persons, people, mankind in an indefinite sense. His bravery line is, We will live in honor, or die like men.
webster_full: MEN, plural of man. Two or more males, individuals of the human race.
1. Males of bravery. We will live in honor, or die like men.
2. Persons; people; mankind; in an indefinite sense. Men are apt to forget the benefactor, while they riot on the benefit.
scriptures: Psalm 4:2
O ye sons of men, how long will ye turn my glory into shame? how long will ye love vanity, and seek after leasing? Selah.
Psalm 9:20
Put them in fear, O LORD: that the nations may know themselves to be but men. Selah.
Acts 17:30
And the times of this ignorance God winked at; but now commandeth all men every where to repent:
1 Timothy 2:5
For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus;
1 Corinthians 16:13
Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong.
corruption_summary: Men is corrupted when the creational plural is emptied, when quit you like men is recast as either brute swagger or a joke, and when the Mediator is replaced by a process between God and a generic public.
corruption_paragraphs: The first corruption is to treat men as a costume. Genesis 1:27 still stands behind the plural: God made them male and female. Late modern talk dissolves the noun into a role you may wear or refuse. Scripture will not. Sons of men in Psalm 4:2 are not a social performance. They are image-bearers in vanity, and they are still men.

The second corruption is to hear 1 Corinthians 16:13 as either a brawl or an embarrassment. The age glamorizes the mocker and then scolds courage as a problem. Paul is not recruiting a mob. He is commanding watchfulness, standing fast in the faith, and strength. Quit you like men is holiness with a spine, not a brand of aggression.

The third corruption is to lose the Man in the middle. First Timothy 2:5 is one God, one Mediator, the man Christ Jesus. Therapeutic religion offers techniques between God and “people.” Political religion offers a cause. The text offers a Man. All men are commanded to repent (Acts 17:30) because that Man is enough for the whole race, and because no other stand-in will do.
roots_summary: Plural of English man. Verse-cache Strong’s on the quotations below: Hebrew ʾîš (H376) at Psalm 4:2; Hebrew ʾĕnôš (H582) at Psalm 9:20; Greek anthrōpos (G444) at Acts 17:30 and 1 Timothy 2:5; Greek andrizomai (G407) at 1 Corinthians 16:13 (quit you like men). No number is added beyond those tags. The companion entry man already treats the singular; this page is the English plural.
roots_lines: Hebrew ʾîš (H376) — man, male, husband (Ps 4:2, sons of men).
Hebrew ʾĕnôš (H582) — man in his frailty (Ps 9:20, but men).
Greek anthrōpos (G444) — man, a human being (Acts 17:30; 1 Tim 2:5, men / the man Christ Jesus).
Greek andrizomai (G407) — to play the man, to act manfully (1 Cor 16:13, quit you like men).
usage: Nations must know themselves to be but men (Ps 9:20) — not gods, and not a law to themselves.
God now commands all men everywhere to repent (Acts 17:30); the audience is the race, not a niche.
Quit you like men (1 Cor 16:13) is watchfulness and faith with a spine, not a costume and not a brawl.
